column1: # Statistics-drift scenarios (Issue #224).
# One scenario per row. Tab-separated. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Columns:
#   scenario  — short id (used for baseline directory name and cache filenames)
#   logfile   — path relative to repo root
#   options   — ltl options (excluding --disable-progress and -o; the cache
#               helper appends -o <logfile> itself when invoking ltl)
# Decision 6 matrix: 4 golden log files x 4 option families, plus the #289
# heatmap pair and the #450 bin-consolidated rows = 21 scenarios.
# Option families (Decision 6):
#   default          baseline raw-array data model on both observed surfaces
#   consolidated     -g 90 changes which samples land in which message bucket
#   bin-data-model   bin-counter data model on both surfaces (honored end-to-end)
#   sorted-by-p999   ranks output by p999 (exercises percentile-based ranking)
#   bin-consolidated (Issue #450)   -g 90 AND the bin-counter data model. This
#                    cross is the only path that reaches merge_bin_counter_entries(),
#                    which projects both sides onto a union geometry — the merge
#                    arithmetic had no baseline behind it before. The merge shows up
#                    in the MESSAGES CSV only: consolidation never touches
#                    bucket-keyed partitions, so this family's STATS CSV is
#                    byte-identical to its bin-data-model sibling and asserts nothing
#                    new. Layer 3 cannot pair the wildcarded consolidated keys, so
#                    Layers 1 and 2 carry these rows — see the l3_unpaired figure.
#   heatmap-raw / heatmap-bin (Issue #289)   -hm duration replaces the terminal
#                    per-time-bucket statistics row with the heatmap row, but the
#                    STATS CSV is a separate render surface — the per-time-bucket
#                    statistics must still be captured and emitted to -o. These
#                    pairs guard that render-surface independence on both models.
# All scenarios pin -mdm and -bdm explicitly (#266 selectors) so the harness
# never relies on internal defaults.
# All scenarios use -cp full (#268) so percentile, shape, and aggregate columns
# emit precise floats. The harness validates against those precise values; the
# human-facing default rounding (-cp default) is not what the harness sees.
# Apache HTTP2 scenarios prepend -du us because its access log records duration
# in microseconds and auto-detection cannot infer this. Without -du us every
# statistic is wrong by 10^k.
